div.head: Ine 50
div.ab: XCIIII. Gif gesiðcund mon þingað wið cyning oððe wið kyninges ealdormonnan for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he þær nane witerædenne, se gesið, forðon he him nolde ær yfles gestieran æt ham.

XCIIII. Gif gesiðcund mon ðingaþ wið cyning oþþe wið his ealdermon for his innhiwum oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oþþe for frige, nah he þær nan witerædene, se gesiþ, forþonðe he him nolde ǽr yfles gestyran æt ham.

Be gesiðcundes mannes geðinge. Gyf gesiðcund mon ðingað wið cyng oððe wið cynges ealdormannum for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he ðar nane witeræddene, se gesiþ, forðon he nolde him ǽr yfeles gestyran æt ham.

Si homo siþcundus agat cum rege uel cum regis aldermanno pro familia sua uel cum domino suo pro seruo uel libero, non habeat ibi aliquam wite redditionem ea uice, quia noluit eos prius a malo castigare domi.

[Be gesiðcundes mannes geðinge.] Gif gesiðcund mon þingað wið cyning oððe wið kyninges ealdormonnan for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he þær nane witerædenne, se gesið, forðon he him nolde ær yfles gestieran æt ham.

{XCIIII} Gif gesiðcund man þingað wið cyning oððe wið kyninges ealdormonnan for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he þær nane witerædenne, se gesið, forðon he him nolde ær yfles gestieran æt ham.

Wenn ein Mann vom Gefolgschaftsstande gegenüber dem König oder dem königlichen Ealdorman für seine Gutsinsassen oder gegenüber seinem Herrn für unfreie oder freie [Schutzbefohlene eine Schuldsühne] abmacht, so erhält er, der Gefolgsmann, nun keinen Antheil am Strafgelde, weil er damals zu Hause ihn [den Schuldigen] an [dessen] Missethat zu hindern unterlassen hat.

If a man of the retainer class makes [a settlement for an offence] with the king or with the king’s ealdorman on behalf of his household, or with his lord on behalf of unfree or free [dependants], then he, the retainer, gets no share of the fine, because he failed at the time to restrain him [the guilty man] from [his] misdeed at home.

If a nobleman comes to terms with the king, or with the king's ealdorman, or with his lord, on behalf of his dependants, free or unfree, he, the nobleman, shall not have any portion of the fines, because he has not previously taken care at home to restrain them [his men] from evil doing.

If a gesith-born man intercedes with the king or the king’s ealdorman or with his lord for members of his household, slaves or freemen, he, the gesith, has no right to any fines, because he would not previously at home restrain them from wrongdoing.

If a nobly born man settles with the king or with the king’s ealdorman on behalf of [a member of] his household, or with his lord on behalf of a slave or a free man, the nobleman does not receive any portion of the fine, because he was unable earlier to restrain him at home from wrongdoing.

In H heisst his: ‘der ihm vorgesetzte Graf’ oder ‘des Königs’; H konnte ‘königlich’ auslassen, da im 10. Jh. jeder Ealdorman königlich war. H modernisiert auch die Endung. — Ines Ealdorman umfasst vielleicht den staatlichen Vogt (s. d. Gl 1) mit

In H his means ‘the ealdorman set over him’ or ‘the king’s’; H could omit ‘royal’, since in the 10th cent. every ealdorman was royal. H also modernizes the ending. — Ine’s ealdorman perhaps also includes the public reeve (see that word in Gl 1)
Q’s familia ‘Hausgenossenschaft, household’ ist zwar anderwärts richtige Übersetzung, scheint aber hier zu eng, da nicht alle Abhängigen des Gefolgsadels unter Einem Dache wohnhaft zu denken sind

Q’s familia ‘domestic community, household’ is indeed a correct translation elsewhere, but seems too narrow here, since not all the dependants of the gesithcund nobility are to be thought of as living under one roof

redditio Q, sachlich richtig gemeint, scheint wegen Gleichklangs mit ræden gewählt. Mit wite synonym setzt dies Kompositum Toller 1247a; -ræden als zweites Glied pflegt ‘conditio, Lage, Verhältnis’ zu bedeuten

redditio Q, correctly meant in substance, seems to have been chosen for its similarity in sound to ræden. Toller 1247a treats this compound as synonymous with wite; -ræden as a second element usually means ‘conditio, situation, relationship’
So begründen andere Germanen den Nichtbezug von Strafgeld und die Haftung (s. d. Gl 6—7d) für Unfreie; Wilda 654. Vgl. Gl Polizei 1C
On the same ground other Germanic peoples base the non-receipt of fines and the liability (see that word in Gl 6—7d) for the unfree; Wilda 654. Cf. Gl Polizei 1C

i.e. before the case passed out of his jurisdiction. Note that a gesiðcund man has a lord. Gesið is here used for gesiðcund man (cf. cap. 23 § 1 above). Liebermann translates his inhiwan by ‘seine Gutsinsassen’ (‘inhabitants of his estate’). If this translation is correct, the last words of the law imply something like the existence of a court leet.

note.label: gesith
note.seg: see p. 396, n. 4. This passage seems to imply that a gesith may have a lord other than the king. The lord envisaged in this passage may be someone to whom the king has granted rights of jurisdiction.
